state.case_summary:
A woman in her late 50s with a history of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia. She had been on methotrexate and sulfasalazine treatment. Initially developed mild aphasia and confusion lasting for several hours. A month later, she developed sudden-onset right leg weakness, which resolved within 2 days. Two months later, she presented with mild headache and right facial droop.

Neurological examination revealed:- Paraphasic errors- Word-finding difficulty- Mild right nasolabial flattening- Bilateral upgoing plantars- No motor or sensory deficits

{'Laboratory Tests': '- Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level- High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody- CSF analysis:   - White blood cell count: 12/µL  - Red blood cell count: 1/µL  - Protein level: 0.055 g/dL  - Glucose level: 58 mg/dL  - 4 oligoclonal bands corresponding to serum sample- Negative results for:  - Rapid plasma reagin  - QuantiFERON  - HIV  - Antiphospholipid antibodies  - Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody', 'Imaging Studies': '- MRI Brain:  Title: Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging  Description: Extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface in the interhemispheric fissure extending over the frontal lobes bilaterally. No acute infarct in diffusion-weighted imaging sequence.- MRA: No vascular abnormality- Chest CT: No pathology or pulmonary nodules', 'Pathological Tests': 'Brain biopsy showed:- Thick exudate in subarachnoid space- Outer portion: necrotic cells beneath arachnoid membrane- Inner portion: lymphocytes and plasma cells with occasional Russell bodies and eosinophils- Multinucleated giant cells between necrotic tissue and viable inflammatory cells- No evidence of vasculitis- Special staining negative for tuberculosis and fungal infection'}

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Idiopathic hypertrophic pachymeningitis
B. Granulomatous Meningoencephalitis of Unknown Etiology
C. Chronic meningitis (e.g., cryptococcal or tuberculous meningitis, though special stains were negative)
D. Rheumatoid meningitis

root.label: Subacute Progressive Multifocal Neurological Deficit with Systemic Inflammatory Features
supporting_facts: History of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia
Previous treatment with methotrexate and sulfasalazine
Initial presentation with mild aphasia and confusion
Mild headache and right facial droop
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
MRI Brain with extensive white matter changes
excluded_candidates: Vascular mechanism: unlikely due to lack of acute infarct on diffusion-weighted imaging and no vascular abnormality on MRA
Infectious mechanism: unlikely due to negative results for various infections and no evidence of vasculitis or tuberculosis on pathological tests
salient_findings: Extensive white matter changes on MRI
